developerPortal: Shopify Dev Dashboard (exact URL not confirmed in research; the partners.shopify.com probe hit a marketing page)
summary: You need your own Shopify OAuth app, because Composio has no managed Shopify app, and every merchant must authorize that app before any end user can connect. The biggest driver of effort is distribution: a multi-merchant agent needs Public distribution, which requires Shopify app review with no published turnaround, and the distribution choice cannot be changed later.

verdict.headline: Shopify needs your own OAuth app, and serving arbitrary merchants requires a Public app that passes Shopify review with no published turnaround.
verdict.timeToFirstConnection: About half a day to one day for a developer with a Shopify partner account, a development store, and the Composio redirect value (estimate, not measured).
verdict.timeToProduction: Plan for roughly 3 to 6 weeks from start to first live merchant (estimate). Review time is the main unknown, and fix cycles after rejection extend it.
verdict.activeEffort: About 1 to 2 days of hands-on work for the app, Composio configuration, install and token code, privacy webhooks, and the listing (estimate).
verdict.approvalWait: No published SLA. Unofficial reports range from about 5 business days to a few weeks, and any rejection restarts the clock.

composio.guidance: You cannot start on Composio-managed auth for Shopify because no managed app exists, so your own Shopify OAuth app is required before any user can connect, including during development. Create a Composio custom auth config now and build against it. You do not switch later, because the custom config is the production path too. Custom configs also give you white-labeling, your own rate limits instead of shared default quota, and custom scopes.

prerequisites.item: A Shopify partner account with access to the Dev Dashboard
prerequisites.why: Client ID and secret are issued from the Dev Dashboard, and the partner account is reported as required to create the app.

prerequisites.item: A Composio account with a custom Shopify auth config, so you have the exact redirect URI
prerequisites.why: The Shopify redirect URI must match Composio's value exactly, and that value is the first thing you need.

prerequisites.item: A decision to use Public distribution for multi-merchant use
prerequisites.why: Custom distribution cannot serve arbitrary merchants, and the distribution choice cannot be changed after you select it.

prerequisites.item: A development store to install into
prerequisites.why: Development stores can host custom-distribution apps and are the normal place to test installs.

prerequisites.item: Publicly reachable HTTPS endpoints for OAuth callback and privacy webhooks
prerequisites.why: Valid TLS is required, and mandatory privacy webhooks must be implemented with HMAC verification.

prerequisites.item: The minimal scope list you need, with a reason for each
prerequisites.why: Apps must request only the access scopes they need, and Shopify may ask for proof of necessity. Protected customer scopes add a separate approval.

stages.title: Register the Shopify app and get credentials
stages.goal: You have a Shopify app with Public distribution, a Composio redirect URI recorded, and client ID and secret stored securely.

steps.text: Copy the redirect URI from your Composio custom auth config for Shopify.
steps.detail: Documented callback value: https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3.1/toolkits/auth/callback. Your dashboard value was not observed, so use what the dashboard shows, character for character.

steps.text: Sign in to the Shopify Dev Dashboard with your partner account.
steps.detail: Docs say Dev Dashboard. Older guides and forums say Partner Dashboard; the current location is the one the Dev Dashboard shows you.

steps.text: Create a new app and select Public distribution.
steps.detail: This choice cannot be changed later. Custom distribution would need a separate app and cannot serve arbitrary merchants.

steps.text: Choose an app name that does not include the word 'Shopify'.
steps.detail: Reportedly rejected in review if it does. Single community source.

steps.text: Copy the client ID and client secret from the app's settings.
steps.detail: Store the secret in a secrets manager. You will paste these into the Composio auth config.

stages.title: Wire the redirect, scopes, install flow, and webhooks
stages.goal: The app's redirect matches Composio exactly, install and token flows follow Shopify rules, privacy webhooks respond, and Composio uses your client ID and secret.
stages.duration: half to 2 days hands-on (estimate) plus no waiting

steps.text: Set the Composio callback as the app's allowed redirect URI, either in the Dev Dashboard or in the auth section of shopify.app.toml.
steps.detail: Must match the Composio auth config's redirect value exactly. A mismatch is the most common setup failure.

steps.text: Draft the minimal scope list with a one-line reason per scope.
steps.detail: Scopes are passed comma-separated in the authorize URL. Flag any protected customer scope separately, because it needs its own approval.

steps.text: Implement the per-store authorize redirect to https://{shop}.myshopify.com/admin/oauth/authorize.
steps.detail: Parameters: client_id, scope (comma-separated), redirect_uri, state. Generate state per request.

steps.text: Implement the token exchange as a POST to https://{shop}.myshopify.com/admin/oauth/access_token.
steps.detail: Body: client_id, client_secret, code. Pass expiring=1 to receive expiring access tokens with refresh tokens. Build refresh-token handling from the start.

steps.text: Make OAuth run immediately after install, before any UI, and again after reinstall.
steps.detail: Required for review. Test both paths later.

steps.text: Make sure installs start from a Shopify-owned surface and never ask merchants to type a myshopify.com domain.
steps.detail: If your flow uses Composio's hosted connect page to collect a store domain, this may conflict. Check this before submission.

steps.text: Use only the GraphQL Admin API.
steps.detail: Required for new public apps as of April 1, 2025.

steps.text: Implement the three mandatory privacy webhooks with HMAC verification: customers/data_request, customers/redact, shop/redact.
steps.detail: Taken from a community source, not yet confirmed against Shopify's official checklist. Confirm before submitting.

steps.text: Paste the client ID and client secret into the Composio auth config and save.
steps.detail: Composio's guide: register the app, set redirect to Composio's callback, then pass client ID and secret.

stages.title: Test installs on a development store
stages.goal: A fresh install and a reinstall both complete through Composio, tokens refresh, and the scopes you need work.

steps.text: Create a development store.
steps.detail: Development stores host custom-distribution apps. Reported limits: free or partner-approved apps only, and up to 10 custom apps per store. Single blog sources for those limits.

steps.text: Connect the development store through Composio's connect flow and complete the Shopify authorize screen.
steps.detail: Confirm the redirect returns to Composio and the connection shows as active. Confirm whether a Public-distribution app can install on a dev store before review. This is not confirmed in sources.

steps.text: Uninstall and reinstall the app, then confirm OAuth runs again.
steps.detail: OAuth must run again after reinstall.

steps.text: Force a token refresh and confirm the connection keeps working.
steps.detail: Access tokens can be short-lived, so verify refresh with expiring=1 tokens.

steps.text: Confirm protected customer fields return data if you requested protected scopes, or confirm they are not needed.
steps.detail: Protected fields are populated only when the matching protected scopes are approved. Sources conflict on whether dev stores bypass manual approval.

stages.title: Submit for review and move to production
stages.goal: The app is Published, and Composio connections work for arbitrary merchants.
stages.duration: 1 to 2 hours hands-on (estimate) plus review wait with no published SLA

steps.text: Write the listing: description, screenshots, and support details.
steps.detail: Reviews of listed apps check the listing content, and thin listings are a reported rejection reason. The agent can draft the text; you supply the screenshots and check the facts.

steps.text: Draft the privacy policy and the scope and data-use justification.
steps.detail: Protected data approval requires stating its purpose and handling. Whether a standalone privacy-policy URL is required is not confirmed.

steps.text: Request protected customer data access if your scopes need it.
steps.detail: Path is unclear: sources say the Partner Dashboard, the Dev Dashboard, or Shopify Support depending on the scope. Confirm in your Dashboard before submitting.

steps.text: Submit the app for review.
steps.detail: Status moves Draft, Submitted, Reviewed (if discussion is needed), Published. Shopify may reject at its discretion.

steps.text: If the status moves to Paused, fix the listed required changes and resubmit.
steps.detail: Paused means a core requirement failed, and you get an email with the required changes.

steps.text: After Published, confirm the Composio auth config uses the production client ID and secret and test one real merchant connection.
steps.detail: Use a real merchant store you control, if possible.

blockers.title: Redirect URI mismatch
blockers.symptom: The Shopify authorize or token step fails, or the connection does not complete, because the redirect URI differs from the one registered.
blockers.workaround: Copy the exact redirect value from the Composio auth config into the Dev Dashboard or shopify.app.toml, then retry. Check for trailing slashes and host differences.

blockers.title: Distribution choice locks you into the wrong path
blockers.symptom: You built and tested a Custom-distribution app, then find you cannot change it to Public.
blockers.workaround: Create the Public app from the start and use it for testing, or accept a separate production app and migrate. Decide Public before writing install code.

blockers.title: Review rejection
blockers.symptom: The app moves to Paused, or Shopify emails required changes.
blockers.workaround: Fix the listed issues, which community sources say are usually OAuth or install-flow problems, billing bugs, missing privacy webhooks, installs that break on a clean dev store, or thin listings. Then resubmit.

blockers.title: Protected customer data access not granted
blockers.symptom: Protected fields such as name, email, phone, or address come back empty.
blockers.workaround: Remove protected scopes you do not need, or submit a justification for the ones you do. Shopify approves only the minimum needed, and refusal is possible.

blockers.title: Cannot find where to request scope approval
blockers.symptom: Docs say the Partner Dashboard holds scope requests, but it may redirect to the Dev Dashboard, which has no API access requests section.
blockers.workaround: Check the Dev Dashboard first. If it is missing, contact Shopify Support for the scope type.

blockers.title: App name rejected
blockers.symptom: Review rejects an app name containing 'Shopify'.
blockers.workaround: Rename the app to a name that describes your product without the word Shopify.

blockers.title: Hosted connect page asks for a store domain
blockers.symptom: Composio's connect page asks merchants to enter their myshopify.com domain.
blockers.workaround: Shopify's rules prohibit asking merchants to type the domain for listed apps. Check the flow before submission, and move the store selection to a Shopify-owned surface.

nuances.text: Distribution is locked once selected. Custom distribution cannot serve arbitrary merchants and cannot charge through Shopify billing.
Unlisted Public apps reportedly have the same review requirements as listed ones. A single forum report says multi-store installs need Public status even when unlisted.
Using your own OAuth app removes the Secured by Composio badge.
Any charges must go through Shopify App Pricing or the Shopify Billing API.
The Shopify accounts discovery document describes an identity login OIDC issuer. It is not the per-store Admin API flow you will use.
The admin.shopify.com authorize probe returned a bot-check page, not a standard OAuth error. It does not show how unknown clients are handled.
Client-credentials grant is only for apps acting on stores in your own organization, so it does not apply to merchant connections.
Review timing comes from unofficial sources. Treat every review-duration figure as an estimate until Shopify confirms it.

agentCanDo: Draft the minimal scope list with a reason for each scope
Check the redirect URI in the repo against the value you paste from Composio
Write the per-store authorize and token-exchange code, including refresh handling
Write the install-flow code that runs OAuth before any UI and again after reinstall
Implement the three privacy webhooks with HMAC verification
Draft the listing copy, the privacy policy, and the scope justification text
Prepare a test checklist for install, reinstall, token refresh, and protected fields
youMustDo: Sign in to the Shopify Dev Dashboard and create the app with Public distribution
Choose the app name and copy the client ID and secret into a secrets manager
Create the development store and install through Composio
Paste credentials into the Composio auth config
Request protected customer data access where needed, through whichever Shopify channel applies
Submit the app for review and respond to any Paused status or reviewer feedback
Decide any legal entity, billing, or partner-plan requirements
